Entries.Title: Start here: files, saved versions, and online sharing
Entries.Purpose: Your project is a folder of files. Git remembers versions of selected files on this computer, so you can see how your work changed. GitHub can host and share those versions online; it is optional for local work.
Entries.Prerequisites: No Git or GitHub knowledge is needed. Choose your own project or use a separate practice folder.
Entries.Effects: Reading this lesson changes nothing. Saving a file in your editor changes that file. Saving a version with Git records selected contents locally. Uploading sends saved versions to a reviewed destination.
Entries.WhenToPause: Pause when you do not recognize the project, the selected files, or the upload destination. The walkthrough explains each change before asking you to review it.
Entries.Example: Edit and save a file → Choose files for the version → Describe the change → Review and save locally → Share online when ready
Entries.Outcome: You can explain the difference between a changed file, a version saved on this computer, and a version uploaded for others.
Entries.Practice: Start the walkthrough and choose "Start the practice project". Make one small change and save one local version. No account or upload is required.

Entries.Title: From a changed file to an uploaded version
Entries.Purpose: Your work goes through four steps: you edit a file, choose it for saving (stage), save a version on this computer (commit), and send it online (push). Save the file in your editor first, so GitCompass can see the change.
Entries.Prerequisites: A practice folder, Git installed, and Allow changes turned on for that folder.
Entries.Effects: Choosing files (stage) only marks them for the next save. Saving a version (commit) keeps a snapshot on this computer. Uploading (push) sends saved versions to the online copy you picked. Edits you did not choose, or did not save in your editor, are not included.
Entries.WhenToPause: Stop if files you did not expect are chosen, you are on the wrong line of work (branch), you have not checked for updates in a while, or a step was left unfinished.
Entries.Example:
git status
git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv
git add -- practice.txt
git diff --cached --no-ext-diff --no-textconv
git commit -m 'Explain the first practice change'
git push <reviewed-remote> HEAD:<reviewed-branch>
Entries.Outcome: A saved version can stay safely on your computer before you upload it. GitCompass only says it was uploaded after checking the online copy.
Entries.Practice: Choose Create a separate practice folder, start saving versions there, edit practice.txt, choose only that file, save one version, and look at the history.

Entries.Title: Choose what belongs in Git
Entries.Purpose: Ignore rules tell Git to skip some files, like build output or private settings. They only affect files Git is not saving yet. A file already saved stays saved, and so do its old versions.
Entries.Prerequisites: Look at the files in your project and decide which ones should never be saved, for example passwords or large generated files.
Entries.Effects: Adding a rule edits a small file called .gitignore. That file can be saved too. Removing an already-saved file from Git is a separate step that keeps the file on your computer.
Entries.WhenToPause: Stop if you see passwords, keys, .env files or very large files. An ignore rule cannot hide a secret that was already uploaded.
Entries.Outcome: Git shows which rule matches when a file is ignored. A file that is already saved stays saved.
Entries.Practice: In the practice folder, create build/output.txt, preview an ignore rule, and check which files it affects before adding it.

Entries.Title: A review request (pull request)
Entries.Purpose: A review request (pull request) asks your team on GitHub to look at your uploaded line of work (branch) and add it to theirs (merge). It is different from Get updates (pull), which downloads new work.
Entries.Prerequisites: Your work is uploaded (pushed), you are signed in to GitHub, and you are allowed to change the project. Know which line of work you want to add to.
Entries.Effects: Making a request creates a page on GitHub for your team to review. It does not combine anything yet, and it does not upload files you have not saved.
Entries.WhenToPause: Stop if your work is not uploaded yet, you are not sure which project or line of work to target, or an earlier request might already exist. Check for an existing request before trying again.
Entries.Outcome: A request appears on GitHub for review. Whether it can be combined may show as pending at first; that does not mean there is a problem.
Entries.Practice: Read this lesson offline. Only make a real request in a practice project your team set up for it.

Entries.Title: Fix clashing changes (merge conflict)
Entries.Purpose: A clash (conflict) happens when you and someone else changed the same lines. Git keeps both versions in the file and asks you to choose. Neither side is automatically right.
Entries.Prerequisites: A combine (merge) that stopped with a clash, the list of files with clashes, your work saved first, and a text editor.
Entries.Effects: Edit each file so it reads the way you want, delete the <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> marker lines, choose the fixed file for saving (stage), then finish the combine. Cancelling (abort) tries to put things back as they were.
Entries.WhenToPause: Stop for pictures, renamed or deleted files, or big clashes, and ask a developer. Always picking one side can throw away work you wanted. Cancelling is not a full backup.
Entries.Example:
git status
git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv
# Resolve a practice text file in an editor, then review:
git add -- practice.txt
git commit
Entries.Outcome: The combine is finished only when every clash is fixed and the combined version is saved, or the cancel is done.
Entries.Practice: Use two practice copies and a practice online copy. Change the same line in both, then combine them and fix the clash.

Entries.Title: Online copies (remotes) and where uploads go
Entries.Purpose: An online copy (remote) is another copy of your project, usually on GitHub. It often has the short name origin. Your line of work (branch) can follow one online line of work for updates, and uploads may go to a different one, for example your own copy (fork).
Entries.Prerequisites: The web address of the online copy, given to you by your team, and the line of work you are on.
Entries.Effects: Looking at these settings changes nothing. Adding an online copy or choosing what to follow changes Git settings for this project, so GitCompass asks you first.
Entries.WhenToPause: Stop if there are several upload places, nothing is being followed, or the online copy has unrelated history. Do not assume every project uses origin and main.
Entries.Outcome: You can see each online copy and which line of work each of yours follows. If GitCompass cannot tell, it says unknown rather than zero.
Entries.Practice: Use practice online copies and compare the one you get updates from with the one you upload to.
